summary.headline: Vardhman Special Steels Q2 FY27 PAT rose about 50% YoY on sales up 27%, with EBITDA per ton at the top of the INR9,000–12,000 guided range.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, with total sales up 27% YoY, revenue from operations up 39% and EBITDA and PAT each up about 50%. Strong automotive demand and tight supply after unscheduled shutdowns at a large competitor drove price increases over the last two quarters, and management said EBITDA per ton is currently at the high end of its range, partly due to inventory gains it called non-sustainable. The greenfield steel plant (INR2,000 crore cost, now expected to be higher), the forging plant and the brownfield expansion from 300,000 to 360,000 tons remain in progress, with the environmental approval still pending. Management also flagged a possible shift to 1:1 debt-equity, a rights issue in 2H CY27, and a possible dividend suspension for 3–4 years, to be decided at the April board meeting.

segments.name: Automotive (core)
segments.commentary: Management expects automotive to remain the core business; a European OE has approved the company and mass manufacturing has started. A major domestic import-substitution grade also got approval, with sales from January 2027.

segments.name: Non-automotive / specialty steel
segments.commentary: Ingot casting for specialty steels starts end-November 2026, with a couple of months to stabilise. Target segments include tool and die steel, oil and gas, railways and bearings, with aerospace and defence later. Management said near-term volumes are very limited given full capacity.

segments.name: Forging (new business, with Aichi as partner)
segments.commentary: Foundation stone laid in July 2026, with the plant expected by March 2028. Full capacity is about 15,000 tons per year, with the first line of about INR450–475 crore, and the Japanese partner Aichi will drive the business. Forging capex is expected to come in below budget.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume now expected at about 260,000 tons, at the higher end of the budget, which management says was about 260,000 tons.
EBITDA per ton guided at INR9,000–12,000 for the foreseeable future, reviewed annually rather than quarterly; management warned Q2 is not sustainable.
Price increases of INR3,500–4,000 per ton were sent by other companies; no settlements yet. Q2 price settlements are still incomplete and Q3 settlements are in progress.

Greenfield steel plant: completion targeted for September 2029 and stabilisation by March 2030. Environmental approval filing expected by December 2026, with the land for the melting part complete and the rolling-part land due by January 2027.

Project cost will exceed the earlier INR2,000 crore estimate. The project design will be finalised by March/April 2027; scope is being built to take output beyond 500,000 tons to at least 700,000 tons in phase 2.

Financing: management is considering 1:1 debt-equity (earlier 0.5:1, maximum 0.75:1), with a rights issue in 2H CY27 and a possible dividend suspension for 3–4 years, subject to the April 2027 board decision.

Capacity: environmental approval currently caps output at 300,000 tons. Application for 360,000 tons has received a committee recommendation, pending final approval. If approved, the increase would take about a year or until December 2027, with capex of about INR100–115 crore.
capex_capacity: Kocks Block and new reheating furnace (commissioned March 2026) took effective capacity to 300,000 tons; output is at full capacity, and rolling mill input capacity is 300,000 tons, giving 270,000 tons output.
New peeling line due early November 2026 and new NDT line due December 2026.
Solar expansion of 22.5 MW (20 MW for the existing plant, 2.5 MW for the NDT line); forging plant solar to be added.
Existing plant capex about INR150 crore; forging plant capex about INR450–475 crore budgeted; greenfield steel capex is being re-estimated, and management declined to give a figure.
Billet length moved from 4.2 m to 5.2 m, improving yield, and production is being stabilised on a single billet size over the next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Demand strong: management cited GST cuts on 2-wheelers and small vehicles, SUV sales, and non-auto demand rising, with a supply shortage after unscheduled shutdowns at a large competitor.
Realisations rising on contractual quarterly price resets, not spot. Management expects average realisation to keep rising for two years.
Management said the market is about 8 million tons and VSSL is too small for significant market share.
Tractor demand slowing, per customer feedback.
Management said no new capacity from competitors is expected in the next two years, but it could be wrong.
Green steel: customers asking about it, with share-of-business benefit visible but no price premium yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA/ton jump came from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is an element of inventory gains but did not quantify it; it is not sustainable. Since the July 2025 move to SAP S/4 HANA, costing is batch-wise, with no period-end revaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth continue above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is seasonally strongest for festive stocking; FY27 volume now expected at about 260,000 tons, at the higher end of the budget.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings and receivables rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings rose to INR162.93 crore due to Ind AS reclassification of LC-discounting creditors; combined with creditors, debt has not risen. Receivables rose with the 11,000-ton incremental sales in August–September, with receivable days up 4–5 days.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and approval for the 300-to-360 KTPA expansion, and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval is still awaited; the timeline is about a year or December 2027, whichever is later, with capex of about INR100–115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Revised capex, payback and forging numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the revised greenfield capex, saying a figure will be shared around April 2027. Forging costs will be lower than budgeted, and initial absorption is about 15,000 tons per year at full capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-auto strategy and near-term volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Ingot casting starts end-November 2026 for tool and die, oil and gas, railways and bearings. Near-term volumes are limited because the plant is at full capacity.

risks_watch: Project implementation risk, which management called the biggest risk, with capex likely to exceed INR2,000 crore and a possible dividend suspension.
Unsettled Q2 and Q3 price resets; competitor letters at INR3,500–4,000/ton are not yet settled, and EBITDA/ton is inflated by inventory gains.
Environmental approval for 360,000 tons is pending with no final letter, and conditions may be attached.
Rising receivables and receivable days, with GST refund cash realisation lagging about 2–3 years (sometimes 3).
New capacity from a listed specialty steel peer (reported to be adding 40–50%), which management said it does not expect to affect the next two years.
Tractor demand slowing, and the new European OE and import-substitution volumes starting from January 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on current demand, pricing and the European OE and import-substitution wins, but cautious and evasive on the greenfield plant's cost, financing, the 360,000-ton approval and forging economics. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers pending April 2027 board and conceptual decisions.
